placements.title: From blocking extraction to receipt-and-observe
placements.frame: What does the caller hold after dispatch, and how does it observe background work without waiting on it or losing it when its receipt is dropped?
placements.why: The position holds that remember returns a receipt in seconds, extraction is watched by a polling cursor, the call never blocks, work survives a dropped receipt, and the agent either polls the run or receives the reaction piggybacked on a later call. Together these state a durable pattern for handing work to the background, not a one-time event, so the theme is one future envelopes can keep feeding. The graph has no existing leaves, so nothing could be reused, and no close-but-not-exact neighbor exists, so this mint stands alone.
consulted: EXISTING GRAPH STRUCTURE: none yet, so no leaf could be reused
Hard rule 2 grain test: the theme (background handoff without blocking) recurs across envelopes; the receipt and cursor are mechanics, not leaves
POSITION VERDICTS: AsyncRememberContract, members src-2, src-3, src-4

mints.name: AsyncJobContract
mints.frame: What does the caller get back at dispatch, what is the agreed way to watch the work, and what survives if the caller stops listening?
mints.title: The async job contract for remember
mints.why: The org names this grouping itself: the 'async job contract' is the ratified term for the receipt-and-poll design. No existing stratum holds it, and the members it will gather (the narrative leaf and the position) are about this one subject across the graph, which is what a thematic stratum groups.

connections.why: The leaf's theme is the receipt-and-observe handoff that the ratified async job contract defines.
The position is the ratified contract itself, holding the receipt, polling cursor, non-blocking call, and dispatch decision.
